messages.text: Arteta: I sabotage our travel plans so players get used to problems

metadata.summary: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says he deliberately sabotaged the club's travel plans during pre-season - to get his players used to difficulties on the road.
metadata.content: Mikel Arteta: Arsenal manager says he deliberately sabotaged his team's travel plans to prepare for difficulties on the road | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Mikel Arteta: Arsenal manager says he deliberately sabotaged his team's travel plans to prepare for difficulties on the road Arsenal were involved in travel difficulties on the way to Naples because of the UK Air Traffic Control incident on Tuesday; Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has revealed he has deliberately sabotaged the club's journey to stadiums, affected meal times and made changing rooms hotter Sam Blitz Football Journalist @SamBIitz Friday 11 September 2026 12:27, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta explains how the club were able to cope with the travel disruption ahead of their Champions League trip to Napoli this week by going through such scenarios in pre-season Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says he deliberately sabotaged the club's travel plans during pre-season - to get his players used to difficulties on the road. Those sabotages include deliberately making his team late for matches by changing their route or meal times - as well as making the changing room hotter and reducing the number of massage beds. The Premier League champions had travel concerns during their trip to face Napoli in the Champions League this midweek, caused by the Air Traffic Control crisis on Tuesday. metadata.summary: American hearts were broken as Elena Rybakina silenced Coco Gauff and the New York crowd to set up a blockbuster US Open final against Aryna Sabalenka, who defeated Jessica Pegula to move a win away from her third straight title at Flushing Meadows.
metadata.content: US Open: Elena Rybakina defeats Coco Gauff to silence New York crowd and set up blockbuster final with Aryna Sabalenka | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open: Elena Rybakina defeats Coco Gauff to silence New York crowd and set up blockbuster final with Aryna Sabalenka Incoming new world No 1 Elena Rybakina silences Coco Gauff and the New York crowd to set up a blockbuster final against defending two-time champion Aryna Sabalenka; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app By Raz Mirza at Flushing Meadows, New York Friday 11 September 2026 06:47, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the US Open semi-final between Coco Gauff and Elena Rybakina. American hearts were broken as Elena Rybakina silenced Coco Gauff and the New York crowd to set up a blockbuster US Open final against Aryna Sabalenka, who defeated Jessica Pegula to move a win away from her third straight title at Flushing Meadows. Rybakina battled back to upset home favourite Gauff 3-6 6-4 6-4 in a fierce semi-final showdown to secure a ​title showdown with defending champion Sabalenka and stay ​on course for a ‌third Grand Slam crown. Sabalenka had beaten Gauff's American compatriot Jessica Pegula 7-5 6-2 ‌earlier in the night to close in on a ​rare three-peat in New York. messages.text: Korda, Corpuz thrash Hull, Woad to make history in tied foursomes session

metadata.summary: Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz created Solheim Cup history with their statement victory over Charley Hull and Lottie Woad in the Friday foursomes, as Team Europe and Team USA shared the spoils in the opening session.
metadata.content: Solheim Cup 2026: Nelly Korda, Allisen Corpuz thrash Charley Hull, Lottie Woad to make history for Team USA in Friday foursomes | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Solheim Cup 2026: Nelly Korda, Allisen Corpuz thrash Charley Hull, Lottie Woad to make history for Team USA in Friday foursomes Team Europe and Team USA both won two points during the opening session of the Solheim Cup in the Netherlands; Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz extended their 100 per cent record together in foursomes; watch live on Sky Sports Golf By Ali Stafford at Bernardus Golf Friday 11 September 2026 11:28, UK Image: Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz made history during the Friday foursomes at the Solheim Cup Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz created Solheim Cup history with their statement victory over Charley Hull and Lottie Woad in the Friday foursomes, as Team Europe and Team USA shared the spoils in the opening session. Hull had won two of her previous three Solheim Cup matches against Korda, including a dominant 6&4 singles victory two years ago, although saw her and Woad dominated by the American pair in the opening match at Bernardus Golf. Korda and Corpuz recovered from losing the first hole to race to a 4&3 victory, seeing them become the first American pair in Solheim Cup history to win five foursomes matches together and the first - from either side - to win five matches in a row. metadata.content: How concerned should big-spending Tottenham be after winless and goalless start to Premier League season? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis How concerned should big-spending Tottenham be after winless and goalless start to Premier League season? Spurs are yet to win or score in the Premier League this season despite a big summer of spending; Roberto De Zerbi's side also failed to have a shot on target last weekend; watch Tottenham vs Everton on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Premier League from 5pm; kick-off 5.30pm Friday 11 September 2026 09:20, UK Image: Tottenham are yet to win or score in the Premier League this season It has been a winless and goalless start to the new Premier League season for big-spending Tottenham. Last weekend's 0-0 draw at Nottingham Forest saw Spurs fail to have a shot on target for the first time in a league game in over four years as they battled to their first point of the season. Roberto De Zerbi's new-look side are yet to click after a £332m summer outlay which saw 10 new players arrive. Having made their worst start to a league season since 2008, Spurs go in search of their first victory on Saturday as they host Everton, live on Sky Sports ​​​​​​.
